articleTitle: Design of Real-time PID tracking controller using Arduino Mega 2560for a permanent magnet DC motor under real disturbances
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The most widely used control strategy in industry is proportional integral derivative (PID) controller. The popularity of PID controllers can be attributed partly to their robust performance in a wide range of operating conditions and partly to their functional simplicity. One of the applications is to control CNC cutting machine model by using permanent magnet DC motor as actuator. In the current work, we contribute to present the design of Real-time PID tracking controller using Arduino Mega 2560 for a permanent magnet DC using Matlab with the intention to both illustrate graphical interface properties using (Matlab GUI) and display the responses of DC motor controlled through PID in real time under real constraints and disturbances. Furthermore, we implement it to the selected Arduino by using Support Package for Arduino Hardware in MATLAB. The speed control implementation of permanent magnet DC motor based on Arduino mega 2560 and L298N H-Bridge as alimentation using PID control method has been validated by experiments on the physical system. Practical results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and advantage of the system control scheme in Matlab in real time. Performance analysis shows the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme in real time.

articleTitle: An Experimental Assessment of Direct Torque Control and Model Predictive Control Methods for Induction Machine Drive
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Finite-State Model Predictive Control methods (FSMPC) have been presented recently in the field of electrical drive and power electronics as an alternative to the conventional strategies. This paper presents a comparative evaluation between Direct Torque Control (DTC) and two finite-state model predictive control strategies applied to induction motor drive. Both DTC and MPC are nonlinear control techniques which dispense with the use of modulation unit (i.e. pulse width modulator (PWM) or space vector modulator (SVM)). DTC can provide good decoupled flux and torque control using pair of hysteresis comparators and lookup switching table for voltage vectors selection. In contrast with the model predictive control which includes the inverter model in control design. The optimal selection of inverter switching states minimizes the error between references and the predicted values of control variables by the optimization of a cost function. The effectiveness of applied algorithms is investigated by an experimental implementation using real-time interface (RTI) based on dSpace 1104.

articleTitle: A Robust Control Strategy for Three Phase Voltage t Source PWM Rectifier Connected to a PMSG Wind Energy Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) has been widely used in variable-speed Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS). Fuzzy logic control (FLC) of the generator side converter (rectifier) has the ability to have a good regulation of the DC link voltage regardless of the disturbances caused by the characteristics of the drive train. The main focus of this paper is to present a model for a voltage source rectifier which is connected to a PMSG in a wind turbine system, where a FLC based on Voltage Oriented Control (VOC) strategy is used to control the mentioned rectifier. The simulation results, using Matlab/Simulink, are presented to show the validity of the proposed model for the PWM rectifier compared to those obtained from the PI controller, and to evaluate the performance of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Circulating Currents Control for Parallel Grid-Connected Three-Phase Inverters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: When connecting two parallel three-phase voltage source inverters between the same DC power supply and AC bus, a zero-sequence circulating current will occur. The presence of these undesired currents increases the power losses and decreases the efficiency of the system. It has been demonstrated that circulating currents are basically influenced by null vectors. In this paper, modeling of the parallel grid-connected three-phase inverters and the cause of the zero-sequence circulating current are presented in detail. Hence, to deal with this issue, a method for suppressing the zero-sequence circulating current based on a PI controller is presented. Simulation results show that the proposed control strategy achieves to effectively suppress the circulating current.

articleTitle: DC-Motor Control Using Arduino-Uno Board for Wire-Feed System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: A speed-controlled dc-motor chopper drive of wire- feed mechanism implemented by Arduino-Uno board is presented in this paper. This drive system is characterized as high static and viscous frictions load, even more it features a variable moment of inertia. Thus, the speed regulator with internal current loop should be carefully designed. Therefore, PI- speed and current regulators design should be fulfilled at limit values that wire-feed mechanism inertia can be taken to insure the stability. Finally, the obtained controllers are discretized and implemented. The experiment results exhibit sufficient agreement in term of transient response and stability which justifies the ability of introducing microcontroller-based Arduino in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Stator Current Demodulation Using Hilbert Transform for Inverter-Fed Induction Motor at Low Load Conditions
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a robust and reliable offline method for induction machine's rotor fault diagnosis, under low load conditions. This method is based on the analysis in frequency domain of the stator current envelope extracted by Hilbert transform. The proposed method, which is one of various demodulation techniques, is theoretically presented then experimentally validated by testing three different induction motors: one in a healthy condition, the second with one broken bar and the third with two broken bars. Each motor is subjected to three load conditions and supplied by voltage inverter which operates at different frequencies. The main results obtained by spectrum analysis of the stator current envelope are compared with these of the traditional MCSA method. The proposed method can successfully detect the fault under various operational situations, even for the lightly load, which makes it more suitable for induction motor fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Based on Sparse Auto-Encoder with MCSA for Broken Rotor Bar Fault Detection and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The understanding of the Broken Rotor Bar (BRB) features frequencies and amplitudes has a great importance for all diagnostic methods. These characteristics frequencies shows a drawbacks under varying load condition. The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) has been widely used to achieve these requirements, because of its efficiency. However, this paper present an enhancing of the fault detection based on a Machine Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) method. Indeed, the use of Sparse Autoencoder (AE) with the combination of Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) shown a good accuracy. Furthermore, the extraction of the new features to use in multi-class classification for the healthy and faulty Induction Motor (IM) is presented.

Author Keywords: Sparse Auto-Encoder Machine Current Signature Analysis

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Power Transformer Oil Using PSO-SVM and KNN Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) and the k nearest neighbor (KNN) classifiers are employed to diagnose the power transformer oil insulation using dissolved gas analysis (DGA). Different vectors are used as inputs for classifiers to achieve a maximum accuracy rate. The five input vectors that are considered: DGA in ppm, DGA in percentage, Dörnenberg ratios, Rogers ratios and Duval triangle reports. Concerning the classes of faults, five types are adopted as output of classifiers (PD, D1, D2, T1&T2 and T3). In order to perform a better fault classification, The SVM parameters have been optimized with a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Using Duval triangle reports, the PSO-SVM algorithm provides the highest accuracy rate than the KNN algorithm one.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Rotor and Stator Faults by Fast Fourier Transform and Discrete Wavelet in Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The purpose of this article is the diagnosis and detection of the stator and rotor faults in induction machine in the presence of the broken bar fault at the rotor level and the stator inter-turn short circuit by two techniques which is an effective solution for the diagnosis of defects. They are based on the signature analysis of the stator current by the fast Fourier transform (FFT) in regime stationary and the analysis by the discrete wavelet transform (DWT). Through the energy stored in each decomposition level obtained by wavelet analysis which gives the advantageous information to decide the situation of each fault and distinguish between the types of faults. The fault signature analysis of the induction machine performed in a healthy and defective state.

articleTitle: Decrease of the resonance phenomenon effect and progress of the piezoelectric sensor correctness
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this work, an equation relates the natural frequency of the piezoelectric accelerometer with the relative frequency of vibratory motion has been proposed to choose the better frequency ratio and reduce the effect of the resonance phenomenon. The simulation results of the model developed have shown that the right choice of the frequency ratio makes it possible to reduce the measurement error and the effect of the resonance phenomenon as well as the increase of the accelerometer accuracy.

articleTitle: Study of Fuzzy Logic controller based MPPT and the P&O for the Z-source inverter integrated in PV system
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The photovoltaic (PV) generation system becomes important as renewable energy sources, due to its advantages such as absence of fuel cost, low maintenance requirement, and environmental friendliness, the integration of the z-source inverter in the (PV) generation system has been very popular among researchers, due to its ability to boost the PV voltage with its single-stage topology. This paper focus on the integration of The Z-source inverter in a photovoltaic (PV) system generation, and the implementation of the Perturb & Observe (P&O) and the fuzzy logic controller algorithm (FLC), to find the Maximum power point (MPPT). At the final we compare the results of the FLC with the Perturb & Observe (P&O) algorithm. A Matlab simulink toolbox and M-file have been used for the simulation, in order to verify the results experimentally. The two algorithm was implemented in a real time with a dSPACE MicroLabBOX, and the I-V curves was programed with Chroma 62150H-600S/1000S Solar Array Simulator.

articleTitle: Global maximum power point tracking of a PV system MPPT control under partial shading
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to control a photovoltaic (PV) generation system under partial shading conditions connected to the grid. The PV generator is connected to the grid through a Grid Side Converter (GSC). In fact, the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is achieved by using the intelligent algorithm for finding the Global Maximum Power Point (GMPP). This algorithm combines a traditional MPPT technique based on Perturb and Observe (P& O) with the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) technique. A hybrid MPPT algorithm is based on the ANN and used to predict the global maximum power point region. Consequently, the (perturb and observe) technique searches for the Maximum Power Point (MPP) in the predicted region. The GSC is controlled in system a way to guarantee a smooth DC voltage with a unity power factor at the grid side. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the control strategies applied to the studied system.

articleTitle: Modelling and Measurement of Electromagnetic Shielding Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In a number of applications in the aerospace industry, electromagnetic fields from various electronic devices may have tremendous effects on each other if proper shielding protection is not appropriately implemented. In this paper, calculated shielding effectiveness SE results obtained by using different physical proprieties will have different electrical conductivity; magnetic permeability and thickness we compared calculated setups. The analytic model presented in this paper is capable of predicting effects also infinite structures are observed.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow for Transmission System with Photovoltaic Based DG Using Biogeography-Based Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: An Optimal Power Flow (OPF) for transmission power system whith presence of photovoltaic based DG (PV-DG) is proposed by this study. We have minimized power losses using Biogeography-Based Optimization method (BBO) by the objective function. This method has determined the optimal PV-DG size and location in a transmission power system. The BBO method has been examined and tested by the modified IEEE 30_bus, and validated by reduced Algerian power system (114_bus) using MATLAB software.

articleTitle: DPC Method For Grid Connected Photovoltaic System Acts as a Shunt Active Power Filter Implemented with Processor in the Loop
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this work, a direct power control strategy is applied to control a photovoltaic system acting as a shunt active power filter. The main task of the presented system is to reduce harmonic currents and to ensure reactive power compensation. Ideally, the presented system needs to generate enough reactive and harmonic current to compensate the nonlinear load harmonic in the line. Therefore, to establish that, a DC-DC boost converter is used to interface the photovoltaic generator with the grid, which provides continuous power flow from the PV to the grid through a voltage source inverter. Moreover, a suitable control for both shunt active power filter and DC-DC boost converter are developed, in order to extract the maximum amount of power from the photovoltaic generator and reduce harmonic currents with insuring reactive power compensation. The co-simulation processor in the loop results show that the proposed control method can inject maximum available power of photovoltaic generator to the grid, compensates the load reactive power, low total harmonic spectrum are effectively achieved, tracks rapid variations of load, and keeps the DC-link voltage constant.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicle Path Tracking Using Nonlinear Steering Control and Input-Output State Feedback Linearization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Autonomous vehicle trajectory tracking field has known a large development in the last previous years especially with the appearance of new efficient control technics. In this paper a new designed controller is used to control the vehicle motion through a predetermined path that considers a different driving scenarios representing a real world driving. In the first part of the work, a nonlinear controller that contains a relationship between lateral errors, heading error and vehicle velocity is designed to generate a suitable steering angle for the vehicle to achieve a good performance in term of path following with minimum distance error. The proposed controller is validated by simulation under different fixed velocities values. In the second part of work, the Input-Output state feedback linearization strategy is used to generate a linear velocity which is used in combination with the obtained steering angle to control the vehicle motion and to minimize the lateral error. The obtained results show a good performance with small distance error compared with the fixed velocities. The stability of the system has been verified using Lyapunov approach.

articleTitle: SOGI-FLL Based Optimal Current Control Scheme for Single-Phase Grid-Connected Photovoltaic VSIs with LCL Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In grid-connected systems, a control that can ensure power flows with better performances and assure the injection of proper power quality into the utility grid is of prime interest. In this paper, an optimum design of a current controller based on Second-Order Generalized Integrator Frequency-Locked Loop scheme (SOGI-FLL) for single-phase LCL-filtered grid-connected photovoltaic VSI is presented. The main aim of this work is to ensure the grid current control with good transient response, injection of proper power quality, and optimization of the computation time. To this end, the SOGIFLL scheme which is characterized by its simplicity, good transient response, and better filtering performances is introduced into the system control. The SOGI-FLL is utilized to estimate proper filtered orthogonal components and frequency of the grid voltage and current to be used by the proposed controller which can enhance its performances. In addition, an improvement in the inner control loops, based on the manipulation of sinusoidal signals instead of dq components through PI controllers is also proposed. This improvement can optimize the computation time by eliminating some PI controllers and dq transformation blocks. Simulation results are provided for a single-phase grid-connected PV, showing the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Improvement of Direct Torque Control Performances Using FCS-MPC and SVM Applied to PMSM: Study and Comparison
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present an improved Direct Torque Control (DTC) for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drive. Nowadays, it is widely recognized that DTC becomes one of the most strategies of control in the industry, because of its known characteristics such as simplicity, minimal torque response time and robustness. However, some limitations in terms of torque ripple and variable switching frequency are exhibited. To enhance this type of control, two techniques have been introduced. The first one is the Control Set Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPTC) which has advantages of being fast with simple implementation, but its switching frequency is variable. The second technique is the DTC control using SVM (Space Vector Modulation), that shows a good performance with fixed switching frequency, which minimizes the ripple torque and improve the THD (Total Harmonic Distortion).

Author Keywords: Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPTC)

articleTitle: Backstepping Sliding Mode Control of a Dual Rotor Wind Turbine System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This article presents a robust control for dual rotor wind turbine system (DRWT) based doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) supplied by a matrix converter. The scientific researches show that a DRWT system could extract additional 20-30% electrical energy compared to a single rotor wind turbine from the same wind speed. The control technique proposed in this work is considered one of the simplest approaches for controlling non-linear systems and systems with an imprecise model. The proposed strategy used in this paper is the backstepping sliding mode control (BSMC). The design of this controller is based on the Lyapunov theorem. Simulation results presented at the end of this article have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed backstepping sliding mode for active and reactive powers control.

Author Keywords: direct vector control backstepping sliding mode control

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of a Doubly Fed Induction Generator Base Wind Turbine System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents modeling and control strategy for a grid connected doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) based wind energy conversion system. Control strategies for the grid side (GSC) and rotor side converters (RSC) placed in the rotor circuit of the DFIG are presented, along with the mathematical modeling of the employed configuration. Firstly, we developed the models of the different elements of the conversion chain and maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control strategy of the DFIG is applied. Moreover, control vector-oriented stator flux strategy of decoupled control of the electromagnetic torque (active) and the reactive powers, to examine the effect of direct Idr and quadrature Iqr rotor currents on real power stator and reactive power Qs and rotor reactive power Qr. Finally, the simulation results of 3MW wind system are presented in a Matlab/Simulink environment. The simulation results are presented and discussed at the end of this paper.

articleTitle: Nonlinear PD control of a Parallel Delta robot: Expermentals Results
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a nonlinear proportional derivative control (NPD) is proposed to solve the trajectory tracking problem of a parallel Delta robot. In order to handle the strong coupling effect and external disturbances as well as to realise high-precision trajectory tracking, the proportional and derivative gains are adapted through time using the tracking error and its time derivative respectively. Experiments are carried out on the parallel Delta-4 robot, and it is shown the effectiveness and the superiority of the NPD controller over the fixed gains PD controller.

articleTitle: Multi-objective System Reliability Optimization in a Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents the use of a multi-objective optimization algorithm for solving the reliability-redundancy allocation problem in case of an overspeed protection system of a power plant. Usually, this kind of problem is considered as a single objective subject to one or several nonlinear constraints and solved by using either mathematical programming techniques or more recently by special metaheuristics. In the present work, the problem is considered as a multi-objective optimization problem. The NSGA-II algorithm is used and demonstrates its ability to identify the set of optimal solutions (Pareto front) providing to the decision maker the optimal solution space.

articleTitle: Design of a MRAC-Based Fractional order PIλDμ Regulator for DC Motor Speed Control
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper deals with the design of a fractional-order model reference adaptive control (MRAC)-based PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup> controller using MIT rule and the ideal Bode transfer function for the speed control of a DC motor. The ideal Bode's model is based on a frequency domain fractional order integrator and the so-called singularity function approximation method is used to convert it into rational function. The designed PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">μ</sup> controller parameters are obtained such that the feedback control system has minimum performance index. Simulation examples illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed PID control adjustment algorithm showing the improvement of the closed loop output behavior.

articleTitle: Performance of Non-Parametric CFAR Detectors in Log-Normal and K Radar clutter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this work, the performance of logt-, GMOS(Geometric Mean Order Statistic), TMOS(Trimmed MOS) and IE-CFAR (Inclusion/Exclusion) detectors are investigated in presence of log-normal and K distributed clutter. First, for a finite number of clutter samples, dependence of the false alarm probability P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FA</sub> upon clutter parameters is examined. The CFAR property for the case of log-normal clutter is maintained while the P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FA</sub> depends somewhat on the shape parameter of the K distribution. Then, by carrying out Monte-Carlo simulations, we show that for the case of log-normal clutter a small detection difference exists between the underlying CFAR detectors. In the case of K-distributed clutter, there is a significant detection difference for small values of the shape parameter (spiky clutter case).

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling and Evaluation of Reparable Electrical Power Supply Systems using Reliability Block Diagram
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper deals with reliability modeling and evaluation of reparable electrical power supply systems. The proposed methods are Reliability Block Diagram (RBD), Minimal Cut Sets (MCS) and Importance factors. These methods ensure quantitative and qualitative analysis of reliability. The MCS are deduced using minimal paths method. Furthermore, various importance factors namely: Birnbaum Importance, Inspection Importance and Fussell-Vesely Importance are applied to identify the most important electric components in the system. The proposed methods are programmed using Matlab software and applied on a Nuclear Power Plant's (NPP) electrical power supply system model. They are validated through the comparison of their results to those obtained by Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) method using RiskSpectrumPSA software. The comparison shows that the results obtained by the proposed methods are very close to those obtained by FTA.

articleTitle: An Improved Observer-based Integral State Feedback (OISF) Control Strategy of Flyback Converter for Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: An improved robust control strategy is proposed in this work to deal with the output regulation control for a DC-DC flyback converter in photovoltaic (PV) system. The control design consists of an observer-based integral state feedback controller (OISF) combined with a standard optimization algorithm. Thus, a PSO algorithm is applied to optimize the OISF controller parameters giving optimal controller gains. In addition, the designed OISF-based PSO algorithm permits to regulate the PV system input voltage such that the PV system operates at maximum power point (MPP). The simulation results obtained under different scenarios clearly demonstrate the effectiveness and improved performance obtained by the proposal (OISF-PSO) scheme compared with conventional PI-based PSO and LQRbased PSO controllers. Also, this improved approach ensures faster tracking of reference maximum power voltage provided by MPPT with a satisfactory performance.

articleTitle: Comparison of PID and Fuzzy Controller for Path Tracking Control of Autonomous Electrical Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this work we present comparison study of application two PID and fuzzy controller to control platonning vehicles. we have two vehicles, the first its controlled by man and the second its controlled lateral and longitudinal by two different controllers. The communication is provided between the two vehicles with exchange information, speed and orientation angle with a fixed safety distance between vehicles. The a kinematic model of vehicles has been described with 3D simulation developed with matlab, Simulink and v-rep software were carried. To approve our approach we have use different reference trajectory. we have used vehicles model in v-rep with communication the speed and orientation angle and our model in simulation. The simulation results illustrate the efficiency of our control design and open the perspectives for future work.

articleTitle: Conducted EMI Prediction in DC/DC Converter Using Frequency Domain Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a simplified approach to predict conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) generated by a DC/DC buck converter in frequency domain. In this approach, the differential mode (DM) and common mode (CM) models take into account the parasitic ringing effect generated during diode's turn-off and MOSFET's turn-off. The switching transients are modeled by two high frequency equivalent circuits and all parasitic elements of interconnects and semiconductor devices are included. Based on the Laplace Transform, the DM and CM models are implemented under SPICE simulator in frequency domain. The CM and DM noise spectrum is obtained rapidly and directly in frequency-domain, the precision of the proposed approach is compared with the experimental results.

articleTitle: High Impedance Faults Location in the Distribution Networks using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The High Impedance Faults are the faults which are difficult to detect. In this paper, a generalized High Impedance Faults arc model is presented. The proposed model is based on anti-parallel diodes with non-linear resistance and DC source connected together. The location of this kind of fault is difficult because it does not cause strong currents. The Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System will be used to localize this type of fault in a network at 24 nodes using a single-phase fault to ground. MATLAB software was used to do all the tests.

articleTitle: Neural Networks trained with Sliding Mode Control for DSIM Supplied by Two Voltage Inverters on Three Levels
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper addresses a sliding mode control (SMC) combined with adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS), the proposed control scheme has been tested for tracking a predefined trajectory by dual-stator induction machine (DSIM). Simulation results show the effectiveness of the investigated scheme.

articleTitle: Cyclic Reports Modulation Control Strategy for a Five Cells Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Multi-cell converters have recently found many applications such as machines control, renewable energies, active filtering and many others. This converter reduces voltage stresses between all cells, which results in lower transmission losses and offers a better harmonic content. This paper proposes a cyclic reports modulation control for a five cells inverter to maintain the floating capacitor voltages to their references and improve the output current waveform. In order to demonstrate the great advantages of the proposed controller it will be compared with the pulse width modulation control.

articleTitle: Synchrophsor Estimation Using The Three-point Interpolated DFT Based On Polynomial Approximation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper investigates the accuracy of the synchrophasor estimator provided by the three-point Interpolated Discrete Fourier Transform (IpDFT) algorithm, which is based on the polynomial approximation of the numerically computed spectrum of the window. The synchrophasor estimation algorithm was tested using two types of windows: cosine and non-cosine windows to meet the accuracy requirements of the IEEE Std C37.118.1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup>-2011 and its amendment IEEE Std C37.118.1a<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup>-2014 under steady state conditions. The test was conducted under the effect of static frequency offsets, harmonic distortion, and wideband noise. The results were found to be accurate and satisfy the M-class PMU requirements under steady state conditions.

articleTitle: Configuration of Three-phase to Eleven-phase Power Transformer
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this paper, the windings configuration of three-phase to eleven-phase power transformer is proposed. Using an optimization technique, Genetic Algorithm (GA) to produce a suitable power conversion with a fixed frequency. The root mean square error (RMSE) criteria is used to minimize the error between the desired eleven-phase output system and the obtained eleven-phase system based on the algorithm. A second criteria is adopted to reduce the number of windings used, which means reducing the construction complexity. The algorithm gives the windings that should be used to create the eleven-phase or multi-phase system and how the windings are connected. For an application, the turn ratio of the windings and their arrangement were found for three-phase to eleven-phase conversion. The simulation of three-phase to eleven-phase transformer has been carried out using the Matlab\Simulink interface. Where it shows the possibility to create a balanced eleven-phase system at the output of the transformer by an appropriate arrangement of windings. The presented approach has the advantage of avoiding the analytical calculation when searching the windings configuration for a large number of output phases.

articleTitle: Influence of Insulating Barrier on the Electric Field Distribution in a Point-Plane Air Gap using COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to calculate the electric field intensity at the plane surface in a point-plane arrangement with the introduction of an insulating barrier between electrodes. We carried out a simulation of a point-barrier-plane arrangement with a point-plane distance of 100 cm. The point is subjected to DC high voltage of positive polarity. Using the numeric finite element method, the geometric model has been implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics® software. This method is used to solve the partial differential equations that describe the field distribution with the presence of space charge. We studied the influence of several parameters of the barrier such as its shape and its number in the interval. To show the effect of the space charge, we considered also a barrier perforated in its middle. We finish by representing the electric field lines and comparing between different arrangements.

articleTitle: Wind Farm Integration Intermittency Impact On Power System Transient Stability
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to study the impact of integrating a large wind power generation on the transient stability issues. We interest to a wind farm connected to a multi-machine transmission power system and we use EUROSTAG as simulation software. The main objective behind this work is to study and simulate various kinds of wind power generator scenarios in the aim to reveal the impact of the integrated wind generation on dynamic performance of power system and on the Critical Clearing Time (CCT) of faults. The Western System Coordinating Council (WSCC) 9 bus and the Algerian islanded power system named Pole In-salah, Adrar and Timimoun (PIAT) 57 bus are used in the simulations. Different case studies are considered during the simulations and the obtained results show the intermittence impact of wind power integration on power system transient stability.

articleTitle: Behaviour of Cross-linked Polyethylene Used as High Voltage Power Cables Insulation Due to Environmental Constraints
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) power cables are increasingly used in power distribution system for their excellent mechanical and electrical performance. Nevertheless, it is well known that degradation under environmental conditions is the major problem in the use of this material as insulation in cables. In this paper, artificial weathering tests on XLPE used as high voltage power cables insulation were conducted. To do so, experiment investigations such as mechanical tests, contact angle measurement and water absorption quantification were used to evaluate the impact of UV and thermal aging on the insulating material properties. In order to highlight the structural changes induced by the constraints, a complementary technique, namely FTIR spectroscopy, was monitored. Results show that UV and thermal aging causes significant evolutions in the XLPE properties.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Synchronverter Virtual Capacitor to Achieve Capacitive Output Impedance
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The remarkable power generation from renewable energy brings out the real need to develop a novel strategy of control with the aim of improving not only the stability but also the quality of power in the same way as for conventional synchronous machine (SM). The synchronverter is an inverter which is controlled in such way as to have a similar behavior to that of SM. The aim of this paper is to develop a strategy of to reduce the rate of harmonic injected to the grid and therefore to improve the synchronverter power quality. Hence, an integral controller is added to force the synchronverter output impedance to be capacitive (named C-synchronverter), this could be done by measuring the feedback inductor current of the filter through an integrator. This latter represents the impedance of a virtual capacitor (Co). The PSO algorithm is proposed to optimize the value of Co in such a way as to minimize the THD of the output voltage.

articleTitle: An Improved Synchronverter based HVDC System Considering Damper Windings Effect
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In recent years, the innovative concept of virtual synchronous machine (VSM) has been adopted in the modern control techniques of high voltage direct current (HVDC) technologies, and in particular, the synchronverter. This latter is originally defined as: inverter that mimics the behavior of synchronous generator is able to keep the entire positive and negative proprieties of a real synchronous machine during steady state and transient conditions. In this paper, a novel control strategy which demonstrate how to include damper windings in synchronverter based HVDC system is described, where both rectifier and inverter sides are controlled in similar way to that of synchronous motor (SM) and synchronous generator (SG) respectively. Simulation testes are performed to show the effectiveness of the proposed strategy of control to achieve high stability performance in ACDC power system.

articleTitle: A New Combined Observer-State Feedback (COSF) Controller of PWM Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Recently, the problem of advanced control design of switched mode DC-DC converters has drawn the attention by several researchers worldwide. In the present work, a new robust controller based Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is proposed in order to control a DC-DC converter. This later is a Combination of Observer-State Feedback (COSF) controller with the PSO optimization algorithm. The proposed controller was tested and compared with two other proposed techniques, Optimized PI (O-PI) and Linear Quadratic (O-LQR) Controllers. The simulation was carried out by means of computational simulations in Matlab/Simulink environment. The obtained results show that the proposed controller exhibits better behavior in terms of settling time, overshoot, robustness, and good tracking.

articleTitle: Conception and Analysis of a Photovoltaic Microgrid in the USTO Campus
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Distributed energy resources increase with strong penetration into electrical systems. The photovoltaic energy of a microgrids has shown great advantages due to the reliable operation of the distribution networks with high flexibility and robustness and also to enable efficiency. In this article, we make a conception of a photovoltaic microgrid that will be installed at the University of Science and Technology of Oran (USTO) in Algeria. This campus is located on a very big area and has a large roofs with flat surfaces. This campus considered as solar energy field offers a great advantage for the photovoltaic energy generation via a microgrid. This article uses hourly solar radiation and temperature provided by the meteorological office to study the radiation distribution and duration of sunshine on campus. This generated PV energy is analyzed in this article with taking into account the roofs total surface of this campus. The consumption of real electrical energy on this campus is given by graphs obtained by the national company of electricity (Sonelgaz), a comparison is made between the generated PV energy and the consumption of real electrical energy. The purpose of this article is to size the installation of photovoltaic panels on the campus and determine the energy provided by the latter and compare it with the actual consumption.

articleTitle: Sliding mode-indirect vector control of double star induction motor using SVM technique
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The Indirect Field Oriented Control IFOC is applied to the Dual Star Induction Motor DSIM. The indirect field oriented control based on Space vector modulation SVM technique is a common solution used to overcome conventional IFOC problems; such as torque ripple and switching frequency variation. However, this control technique relies on the orientation of the rotor flux and the PI controllers. The actual article based on improving the performance of SVM-IFOC by using the sliding mode controller SMC instead of the PI controllers. This controller can solve the classic PI problems which are represented in robustness with respect to the variation of the parameters and the external disturbances and gives excellent dynamic performances in a game of speeds. Furthermore, the mode controller is based on a strategy with a sat' function to reduce the chattering effect. The effectiveness of the wholecompound control method (SVM-IFOC by sliding mode controller) is studied in different robustness tests with simulation using Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Hybrid PV-Wind based water pumping system optimum sizing: a PSO-LLP-LPSP optimization and cost analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This article presents the results of a developed hybrid PV/wind water pumping optimization sizing method, taking into account the strong combination between the intermittent energy resource (solar and wind), the water storage capacity and a given load profile. This optimization method is based on the use of metaheuristic technique. This algorithm, often inspired by nature, is designed to solve complex optimization problems. Among the most used metaheuristic, we used the Particle Swarm optimization algorithm (PSO), considering the Loss of Load Probability (LLP), Loss of Power Supply Probability (LPSP) criteria and the system cost indicator. The suggested method determines the system optimum configuration, which can achieve the desired LLP and LPSP with minimum cost. To reach this aim, an objective function is formulated for the system cost. It must be kept to a minimum while respecting the reliability constraint. The effectiveness of the PSO in solving a hybrid system optimization problem is scrutinized and its performance is analyzed. To highlight the propounded method performance real case studies have been conducted and the results are discussed.

articleTitle: Composite Insulators in a 400 kV AC Line in Algeria for Improving Electric Field Distribution
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Composite insulators are widely used in the 60 and 220 kV transmission lines in Algeria. The reliability of these lines has been improved which leads us to think of integrating this type of insulators in the 400 kV transmission lines recently introduced by the Algerian Company of Electric Power and Gas (SONELGAZ) where glass insulators are used. Thus, in this paper, we evaluated at first the electrical performances in terms of electric field distribution on three proposed composite insulators with different shed configurations under different surface conditions (dry and clean, uniformly polluted and in presence of water droplets). Then, we compared the electric field distribution of the selected composite insulator to the already used made of glass in the 400 kV AC line of TILGHEMT-DJELFA in Algeria under normal and contaminated surface conditions. Using 2D simulation, composite insulators presented better electric field distribution. Finally, the generated heat along insulator surface is estimated for both composite and glass insulators under different surface conditions. Note that an appropriate corona ring is used at both HV and ground ends for glass and composite insulators with constant parameters (corona ring diameter, corona ring tube diameter and corona ring height) throughout the whole study.

articleTitle: Evaluating semi-empirical models for global solar radiation on inclined surfaces in south of Algeria
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In the present work, we studied some theoretical models to estimate the components of solar radiation received at ground level. These models take into account the effects of scattering and absorption of solar radiation during its passage through the atmosphere. They are based on the determination of transmission coefficients of different atmospheric constituents. These factors require the availability of current meteorological parameters (relative humidity, air temperature, atmospheric pressure...etc.) and geographical parameters of the considered site as latitude, longitude and altitude. In this work we propose to estimate global solar radiation in two sites of Algeria: Tamanrasset and Ilizi. For this purpose three models are used: Lacis&Hansen, Lieu & Jordan and Capderou models Models were compared on the basis of statistical error tests using the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), the root mean square error (RMSE).

articleTitle: PIL Test for Voltage Source Inverter control used in Off-grid PV system
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper treats the case of the off-grid photovoltaic (PV) system, feeding a three-phase resistive load and working only during sunlight availability. In this case, backup batteries are not used. So, no charge controller is needed, neither any DC-DC power converter as long as the PV generator (PVG) delivers a voltage greater to a certain value that keeps good functionality of the inverter. Thus, this PV chain is reduced only to PV array and three-phase voltage source inverter (3-ph-VSI), followed by (delta/wye) transformer. The discrete virtual Phase Locked Loop (PLL) is used to generate a fixed frequency (50 Hz). The proposed system topology allows designing a low cost system, and providing necessary power that can meet the daytime load demand. Next, Processor in the Loop (PIL) method is performed in order to test the hardware implementation of the inverter control algorithm already simulated with MATLAB/ Simulink. This is done by creating the PIL block which will be run in the STM32F407-VG discovery board, while the plant model will be simulated in the host computer. The ST-LINK communication interface is used to connect the host computer to the embedded board.

articleTitle: Optimal Dynamic Equivalence Based on Multi-Objective Formulation
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In the last decade, dynamic equivalents gain a great attention by researchers. Generally, replacement of the external system is based on the preservation of power flows at tie lines or preserving the electrical power of the generators in the internal system closely. To achieve both objectives, a multi-objective formulation is proposed. For this purpose, the novel Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA) is used to drive Pareto set of optimal solutions. Then, a Fuzzy-Based selection mechanism is employed to find the best compromise solution that satisfies both objectives. In order to fit the dynamics of the external system, a six-order detail model with excitation system is used for an explicit representation. Applications are carried out on the New England system and the quality of the estimated model is validated through several scenarios.

articleTitle: Impact of the Used Chaotic Map on the EMI Reduction Level
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The chaotic pulse width modulation (CPWM) is a spread spectrum technique that plays an increasingly important role when tackling the electromagnetic interference (EMI) problem. It has proven to give interesting results in terms of EMI levels reduction. The EMI noise reduction in the chaotic modulation is a function, among others, of the initial value. In fact, each chaotic map can exhibit different modulation effects with different initial values. This paper is an attempt to harness the benefits of the chaotic digital control when tackling the EMI problem in a boost converter. Different chaotic maps were analyzed and the effect of the chaotic map on the EMI reduction level was highlighted.

articleTitle: Optimal Combined Dynamic Economic and Emission Dispatch Including Wind and Photovoltaic Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper attempts to propose an optimal solution to the Combined Dynamic Economic and Emission Dispatch (CDEED) problem including wind and photovoltaic power systems considering the environmental benefits. The optimal dispatch modeling problem was formulated using the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The PSO tool was used for solving the nonlinear programming problem. The proposed appraoch easily takes into account different compromise between the dynamic fuel cost dispatch with the valve-point effect and the emission gas exhaust subject at two different case of participation of both photovoltaic and wind units. Simulations were performed firstly over three units power system, then various scenarios are also performed using the IEEE 13 units test system. The obtained results confirm the robustness and validity of the proposed methodology through a comparative study over other published approaches.

articleTitle: Implementation of new adaptive power-split management strategy in a battery-super capacitor electric vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The present paper deals with a real time implementation of a new adaptive frequency-based power management strategy of a small-scale hybrid battery-super capacitor system, dedicated to an electric vehicle. The ultimate objective of the strategy is to ensure a smart use of the two sources, improving as a consequence both the autonomy and the system lifetime. To do so, and unlike the conventional power frequency separation technique, the filter adapts its pass band frequency to keep the charge's state of each source in a tolerable range and provides power amounts to the load demand. The experimental results demonstrate that the system commutates smoothly between the operating modes, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed control techniques.

articleTitle: Reliable, efficient and fault tolerant power converter for grid-connected PV system
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this paper, a grid-connected PV system for a three phase renewable energy integration applications is investigated. Efficient power topology and control algorithm designs aiming to optimize the performances of this power conditioning system are presented. The proposed two stage installation aims to optimize its reliability and efficiency and to be fault tolerant to one power switch fault. The first is a DC/DC conversion stage based on two boost reconfigurable converters controlled with a Distributed MPPT algorithm. The efficiency of each of the converter configuration and its MTBF (Mean Time Between Failure) are calculated using the Reliability theory and the MIL-HDBK-217F standards. Thanks to an appropriate bi-objective function optimization, the DC/DC configuration that maximize both its efficiency and reliability is chosen. Finally, we propose to integrate a fault tolerant 3 level NPC converter for the second power stage of the proposed grid-connected PV system. Simulation results carried out with a 10-kVA system are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Real-Time Hybrid Control of Induction Motor Using Sliding Mode and PI Anti-Windup
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a combined hybrid command between the sliding mode and PI Anti-Windup applied for the speed pursuit of an induction motor, the nonlinearity of their mathematical model increases the conception complexity of a powerful controller, the conventional methods cannot guarantee good performances in the presence of structural or external disturbances. The advantage of using sliding mode control is the simplicity of the design and their insensitivity to parametric variations. But the chattering phenomenon appeared in the steady-state remains an obstacle limits the application of this technique. We proposed to use a PI Anti-Windup regulator for control in the steady-state, however, the sliding mode regulator will work during the transient regimes, where a classical supervisor can handle the transition from one controller to another via approximate information on the operating regime. Experimental results are presented and analyzed to justify the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Optimized PID for Direct Power Control with an improved LCL filter design using GWO for Three-Phase Inverters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents analysis and control of three-phase inverter for renewable energies sources and for Micro-Grid (MG) purpose using the Direct Power Control (DPC). The proposed control is based on the variation of instantaneous active and reactive power errors in the virtual dq references frame and optimized Proportional-Integral-derivative (PID) controllers. Moreover, the grid synchronization is carried out using Double Second-Order Generalized Integrator (DSOGI) to ensure correct orthogonal signals generation. Also, a DC link voltage controller has been performed to ensure the power balance between the source and the power injected to the grid through LCL filter which parameters were also optimized. In this paper, a new objective function is formalized and proposed to enhance the generated power quality. The recent algorithm Grey Wolf optimizer is performed for the first time to resolve the optimization problems for the overall system.

articleTitle: A neural network architecture for automatic and objective surgical skill assessment
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Improving surgical skills through various training programs is critical for healthcare. To reach this goal, it is important to increase the reliability of surgical skills assessment. In this paper we propose an objective and automatic procedure to evaluate the performance of trainees on three different tasks: Knot tying, needle passing and suturing. The core of the evaluation procedure is a fully connected deep neural network with three hidden layers and twenty nodes for each layer. The network is trained exclusively on expert database by assuming the tasks being already known and classified. Our framework is then used to evaluate intermediate and novice trainees by providing scores referenced on the performances of the experts. The results show experimentally the ability of our network architecture to automatically evaluate classified surgical tasks.

articleTitle: Fault-tolerant control of asynchronous machine taking into account faults
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper proposes a simple and effective technique that allows fault tolerance of the converter-machine assembly. The proposed approach is based on Lyapunov theory. This work describes a study of the different fault modes of a converter-machine system. To this end, we present a method for the three-phase modeling of the asynchronous machine (ASM) in the presence of a short-circuit fault between coils of a stator phase. This method is based on the theory of electromagnetic coupling of electrical circuits. The proposed control is verified by numerical simulation. The results of the numerical validation demonstrate that the good functioning of ASM in the presence of both faults.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Control of Multi-Phase Induction Machine Drives Based on Cascaded Hybrid Multi-level Inverters
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a new control strategy based on a fuzzy logic controller (FLC) for multi-phase induction machine (MPIM) drive supplied by cascaded hybrid multi-level inverters (CHMI). So, two control techniques are presented and compared: the first one is based on a linear PI controller while the second one is based on a nonlinear FLC. The analysis and comparison of the simulation results of the FLC and PI controllers clearly show that the FLC ensures better performances and good robustness than the PI controller applied to the electrical drive based on CHMI.

articleTitle: Impedance nature of long horizontal grounding electrode employing TLM
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This investigation is devoted to analyse the impedance behaviour of long horizontal grounding electrodes as function of frequency for several soil resistivity values. The real and imaginary parts of grounding impedance have been analysed in order to characterize its nature at several points along the electrode. We show that the impedance increase reflects its inductive behaviour. This impedance increases with the grounding electrode length. For high soil resistivities, resonant peaks appear. They are attenuated with the electrode length increase.

articleTitle: Numerical study using FVM of three cavities within XLPE insulation of HV cables
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The presence of cavities inside cross-linked Polyethylene (XLPE) insulation cable essentially affect the electrical filed distribution in insulating part of power cable. Indeed, internal partial discharges (PD) in theses cavities induced degradation of dielectric properties, which instigate insulation ageing and may lead to cable failure. Therefore, this paper studies the behavior of electrical constraints within XLPE insulation containing cavities. The purpose of this work is based on numerical resolution of Laplace equation using the finite volume method (FVM).

articleTitle: Field Oriented Control of Doubly Fed Induction Generator Integrated in Wind Energy Conversion System using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Nowadays, the Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) is increasingly used because of its advantages in better reliability and supply division. This paper presents the application of a simulation with a proposed model and control of a (DFIG) integrated into a wind energy conversion system with a variable speed wind turbine. Firstly, a mathematical model of the machine written in an appropriate d-q reference frame is proposed to investigate simulations. secondly, and in order to control the power flowing between the stator of the DFIG and the power network, a control law is synthesized using two types of controllers: Proportional-Integral (PI) controller and neural networks (NN) based controller. finally, their respective performances are compared in terms of power reference tracking and robustness against machine parameters variations.

articleTitle: Vibration suppression for flexible satellite during attitude stabilization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper treats the problem of vibration mode and attitude control stabilization of a spacecraft with flexible appendage based on state feedback controller (SFC) and vibration suppression using disturbance observer (DO). The spacecraft has a central rigid body and large flexible appendage. The unwanted coupling torques in attitude dynamics that is generated by the vibration of large flexible appendage can affect the performance of attitude stabilization systems. By intergrading DO with SFC, the vibration torques can be reduced and the performance of the desired dynamic can be guaranteed. The Simulation results for flexible spacecraft are given to demonstrate the excellent performance of the composite control approach.

articleTitle: Experimental and numerical modeling of corona discharge generated in an electrostatic precipitator
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The present article is devoted to the numerical and experimental study of positive and negative corona discharge in air at atmospheric pressure in a multi-wire-to-planes geometry, which is widely exploited in the design of the electrostatic precipitator (ESP). A detailed experimental procedure was carried out on a scaled-down laboratory prototype developed for the purpose to determine the corona discharge characteristics. Different electrode layouts have been tested to improve the performance of the precipitator. In addition, the corona governing equations are successfully implemented and solved using Comsol Multiphysics. It has been found that the level and polarity of the applied voltage as well as the geometrical parameters of the studied configuration have a very significant influence on the intensity of the corona discharge current.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analyzing Energetic Hysteresis Classical Model
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The Jiles-Atherton model (JAM), developed by Jiles and Atherton, and the energetic model (EM), developed by Hauser are two phenomelogical models of hysteresis that are usually used in ferromagnetic material like FeSi(3% Si).In all previous works the measured hysteresis curve is identifiable by the EM, and the corresponding parameters of the JAM can be calculated. The other way is not easily and unequivocally possible because the EM uses more parameters. In our work we have used two simple methods for identification of the EM parameters with the hysteresis curve of the JAM. Also the obtained measurement with Eipstein frame that give us in the majority of the cases only the major hysteresis curve and we have to use another manner to find the Anhysteretic curve.In our case we have used JAM hysteresis mode to obtain the Anhysteretic curve that is very important in EM parameters identification with nonrecursive and recursive methods based on linear least-square minimizations (LLSM).We study in the end of the paper the influence of various model parameters on the shape of hysteresis loop. For this purpose we decide to focus on each parameters of energetic model (EM).

articleTitle: Control and Monitoring of Electrical Embarked Network with Cloud Technology using Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Electrical embarked network can be described as strongly coupled multi-sources, multi-loads systems. This system can be affected by a long overload or frequency variations. However, if these disturbances cannot be controlled or isolated in a short time, they will be responsible for a lots of energy crisis. So, in this paper, we describe a prototype of smart electrical protection device that can be used to control and monitoring a typical electrical embarked system by Ethernet network at anytime and anywhere. This embarked system will be controlled by programmable logic controller Zelio Schneider and embedded system Raspberry Pi. Moreover, the communication between these two parties will done by sending data from the website to our electrical system by Json-file and store data in cloud database server. For any fault or change of data estimation in our system, the smart electrical protector sends a message and musical alert to website which can be changed automatically without refresh.

articleTitle: Implementation of Modified SVPWM for Three-level Inverter Using STM32F4
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel strategy realization of the three-level Space-Vector Pulse-Width Modulation (SVPWM): an implementation of simplified algorithm SVPWM for the three-Ievel inverter. Due to the geometrical symmetry of six sectors, there exists close relationships between on time calculations and on time arrangement for switches of the inverter. Therefore, this symmetry can be extended to the remaining sector based on single computation being done for the first sector only. Consequently, compared with the conventional algorithm, the proposed algorithm is more suitable for hardware implementation by greatly reducing computations. Similar configurations are mostly implemented using either DSP card or Dspace platform, which increase the cost of the system. This paper develops the above strategy of simplified SVPWM algorithm using Matlab/Simulink software investigating the use of a cost-effective card and the flexibility of STM32F 4 discovery board. The obtained results witness the ability of STM32F 4 in the control a T-type three-level inverter.

articleTitle: Unit commitment using dynamic programing for planning optimization and emission reduction
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper presents a dynamic programing method for solving unit commitment (UC) problem considering the profit maximisation and emission minimisation. The UC problem is considered as tow linked optimization sub-problem: the unit-scheduled problem that can be solved by the DP method for the minimization of the transition cost, and the economic dispatch (ED) problem that can be solved by the lambda iteration method for minimization of the production cost. The studied system consists of 10 thermal units, PV system, a wind plant in order to minimize the CO2 equivalent emissions of gas turbines.

articleTitle: automatic language identification for berber and arabic languages using prosodic features
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This paper describes the design of an automatic identification system for the distinction between two common languages in Algeria which are MSA (Modern Standard Arabic) and Kabyle which is an Algerian Berber dialect. The characteristics used for this are prosodic (melody and stress) and cepstral (Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients) features extracted from a bilingual database formed by combining two databases. For the classification step Support vector machines are trained for language modeling because it is a recognition of two languages which puts him in a better position to establish this task. Experiments have shown the superior reliability of our system when using both types of characteristics when compared to the use of each type separately. It was found that when using prosodic characteristics the system gives an encouraging rate of 95.42% which was improved to 95.83% when adding acoustic features and 97.5% (so an improvement of 1.67%) when combining prosodic and acoustic features which has shown the superiority of this vector over those previously cited.

articleTitle: The effect of facets reflectivity on the static characteristics of (DFB) semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: In this paper, we present a rigorous approach based on split-step time-domain dynamic modeling (SS-TDM) algorithm using to solve the time-dependent coupled wave equations of the time-domain traveling-wave (TDTW) model to investigate the effect of facets reflectivity on the Light-Current characteristics of (DFB) semiconductor laser for different values the coupling coefficient. The simulation results show that using high reflection coating on the front facet and low reflection coating on the back facet with a proper diffraction grating can significantly improve the power-conversion efficiency of the (DFB) semiconductor laser.

articleTitle: Primary Arc Modeling in Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: According to the previous research, fault arcs can be modeled numerically under a simulation program such as Matlab - Simulink. In this paper the dynamic behavior of the arc is represented as a time-varying resistance by solving a differential equation of arc conductance as a function of energy balance in the arc column. Depending on the variation of the arc parameters, certain effects of the interaction with the transmission system are observed.

articleTitle: Leader-follower formation control using PI controller
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to study the leader follower formation control problem of non-holonomic mobile robots. The trajectory tracking control for a single non holonomic mobile robot is extended to the formation control for two non-holonomic robots in which one is the leader and the second is the follower, based on PI control technic. Simulation results are presented which demonstrate the good performance of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: A neutral point balancing problem in a three Level inverter analyzed using a redundant Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: Over the past few decades, the fast development of high switching frequency power electronics drives towards wider application of voltage source inverters in AL power generation. Thus, a modulation technique with less total harmonic distortion, fewer switching losses, and wider linear modulation range, was needed. An analyze of the potential variation of middle point for three level inverter and based on redundant small vectors compensation, we have proposed the action time correction methods for the basic voltage vectors and the original fundamental voltage vector This study, afford a contribution to the problem of neutral-point voltage balancing in three-level NPC converter. That showed the three-level neutral point potential fluctuations can be suppressed effectively by the middle point potential compensation algorithm. MATLAB was used to build a simulation model for analysis.

articleTitle: Loop-Shaping Control Design Of Boost/Cuk High Voltage Gain For Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The main objective of this work is to propose the Loop-shaping command of a high gain boost converter with amid point from the solar panels. The efficiency of energy conversion is improved by using a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller. The DC-DC converter uses a single switch to obtain a hybrid DC / DC converter. This will allow symmetrical voltages in applications with half-bridge single-phase inverters. The application of Loop Shaping control ensures robustness against model uncertainties and unmeasured disruptions, providing a systematic framework for synthesizing controllers that meet performance objectives. This energy conversion structure is simulated using the PSIM software.

articleTitle: Design Of an integration Frame HAZOP-SIL for safety Optimization of a Fired Heater
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The paper highlight the guidelines to propose an integration frame to optimize the saety of a fired heater F100200 located in CDU unit (crude distillation unit) in ADRAR refinery south of Algeria.The proposed frame integrate the HAZOP - hazards and operability studies and safety integrity level studies. The idea behind the proposed method is to overcome the limitations raised from the application of each technique alone. The application of this proposed technique in the fired heater indicate that the heater needs more safeguards to work in a safe manner, as a conclusion more safety instrumented functions should be added, and the safety level of the existing ones should be checked.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Algorithm by Combination of Genetic Algorithm and Local Optimization for Constrained MHD Pump Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The pumping of liquid metals by magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) converters, without any moving parts are competing with conventional hydraulic pumps. Thus, the movement of the fluid is a consequence of the interaction the magnetic and electric fields. This work relates to the application of an approach for optimal design of a DC magneto-hydrodynamic pump. The optimization method is based on the solution of non-linear constrained problem by combination global and local optimization method. This paper applies the hybrid algorithm by combination of genetic algorithm and Fmincon for optimal design of DC MHD pump. The comparative study of the obtained results shows that the performance of the hybrid method is effectively improved.

articleTitle: Optimal Reactive Power Flow In The Presence of Wind Power For Active Power Loss Minimization
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: This study proposes a solution to the optimal reactive power flow (ORPF) in power systems incorporating wind power. Two aspects are studied in this paper. The first one is the technical aspect, includes the real power loss reduction, which presents the main objective of this work. The second is the economic aspect, considers the optimal wind power and FACTS devices investment cost. The autonomous group particle swarm optimization (AGPSO) optimization technique is employed and compared with improved and modified particle swarm optimization (IPSO & MPSO) for solving the proposed ORPF problem. The Algerian power system 59-bus systems are used as test systems. The simulation results obtained from the proposed algorithm shows that this algorithm is capable to give higher quality solutions to solve the optimal reactive power flow problem.

Author Keywords: wind power and FACTS devices cost

articleTitle: LCL Filter Design Optimization for LV Modular Multilevel Converters in Hybrid ac/dc Microgrids Application
publicationTitle: 2018 International Conference on Electrical Sciences and Technologies in Maghreb (CISTEM)
abstract: The optimization design of a LCL filter associated with the arm inductor of a LV modular multilevel converter used as an interlink converter in a hybrid ac/dc microgrid is presented.
